examples.question_text:
A mobile mechanic uses the model $C = 70t + 95$, where $C$ is the charge in dollars and $t$ is the time worked in hours.

a. State the gradient and explain its meaning.
b. State the vertical intercept and explain its meaning.
c. Predict the charge for $3$ hours of work.
examples.solution_text:
a. The gradient is $70$ dollars per hour. Each additional hour of work increases the charge by $\$70$.

b. The vertical intercept is $95$. The fixed call-out fee is $\$95$, before any hours of work.

c. $\begin{aligned} C &= 70(3) + 95 \\ &= 210 + 95 \\ &= 305 \end{aligned}$

The predicted charge is $\$305$.

examples.question_text:
The volume of water remaining in a tank is modelled by $V = 2400 - 400t$, where $V$ is measured in litres and $t$ is measured in hours after draining begins.

a. Interpret the gradient and vertical intercept.
b. Predict the volume after $2.5$ hours.
c. Determine when the model predicts an empty tank.
d. Calculate the predicted volume after $8$ hours and explain the limitation.

A child's height was measured between ages $3$ and $9$. Over this interval, the height is modelled by $H = 5A + 82$, where $H$ is measured in centimetres and $A$ is the age in years.

a. Predict the height at age $6$ using interpolation.
b. Predict the height at age $15$ using extrapolation.
c. Explain why the prediction at age $15$ may be unreliable.
examples.solution_text:
a. $\begin{aligned} H &= 5(6) + 82 \\ &= 30 + 82 \\ &= 112 \end{aligned}$

The predicted height is $112$ cm. Age $6$ is within the measured interval, so this is interpolation.

b. $\begin{aligned} H &= 5(15) + 82 \\ &= 75 + 82 \\ &= 157 \end{aligned}$

The predicted height is $157$ cm. Age $15$ is outside the measured interval, so this is extrapolation.

c. The model assumes growth of $5$ cm per year. Growth can change during puberty, so measurements from ages $3$ to $9$ do not establish that this rate continues to age $15$.

coverage.summary: Authored three worked examples covering all distinct assessed methods with changed values and supplied booklet methods. Assessments were classified only; their mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Questions and solutions are separate, prose remains editable, and solution ink inherits the renderer's blue. The tank diagram contains solution-only annotations and specifies 10 pt black labels. Actual rendering and final-size visual verification remain for the later capture stage.

examples.derivation: The coefficient 70 represents a charge increase of $70 per hour; the constant 95 represents the fixed call-out fee. Substitution gives C = 70(3) + 95 = 210 + 95 = 305 dollars. This follows the supplied contextual interpretation and substitution methods. No diagram is necessary.

The gradient is -400 L per hour and the initial volume is 2400 L. At 2.5 hours, V = 2400 - 400(2.5) = 1400 L. Setting V = 0 gives 400t = 2400 and t = 6 hours. At 8 hours, V = 2400 - 3200 = -800 L, which is physically impossible. The solution diagram joins (0,2400) and (6,0), matching the model and its stated draining interval. Its derived annotations occur only in the solution.

At age 6, H = 5(6) + 82 = 112 cm; age 6 lies within the measured interval 3–9. At age 15, H = 5(15) + 82 = 157 cm; age 15 lies outside that interval. Puberty can change the growth rate, so the measured interval does not establish continued growth of 5 cm per year. This follows the supplied height-model limitation exercise and explicit syllabus coverage. No diagram is necessary.
